content:
alex: Heads up - customer C-998 reported sharp p95/p99 regressions for text-gen starting ~04:20 UTC. No increase in qps. Error rates unchanged. Ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/998
nina: which model/region?
alex: model redwood-small-v1 in us-west-2. baseline p95 ~110ms, yesterday spiked to ~420ms and p99 to ~1.9s. timeline attached in ticket.
rahul: I pulled runtime logs and GPU allocator logs. Pattern: steady increase in per-session KV entries over hours, free gpu-memory broken into many small fragments. allocator reports many small cudaMalloc retries. No node OOMKills.
dave: that smells like fragmentation + kv cache growth (sessions never evict). Do we have session TTL for this customer?
alex: they use long lived sessions for chat (no TTL), and send many small streaming appends.

rahul: repro on staging (script attached):
1) start 50 sessions to the model with context_len=8192
2) every session sends 1-4 token appends every 1s for 45 minutes
3) monitor allocator metrics and token latency

rahul: commands I used:
```
# realtime allocator logs
kubectl logs -l app=inference-worker -n inference --since=1h | grep allocator
# metric samples
curl http://metrics.local:9090/api/v1/query?query=allocator_fragmentation_ratio
```

nina: logs snippet:
```
2028-07-11T04:22:11Z warn allocator: small block alloc fail, retries=6, requested=32MB
2028-07-11T04:22:11Z info kvcache: session hit table grow: 2048 entries
2028-07-11T04:22:12Z warn spill: spilling 24MB to host due to alloc_retries
```

dave: so runtime falls back to host spill / CPU copy which explains extra latency even though not OOM.
ops-bot: note: earlier incident 2028-06-01 had similar allocator fragmentation, fixed by rolling restarts.

nina: immediate mitigations we can apply without heavy churn?
- enable session eviction TTL for that customer (30s)
- throttle append frequency at API gateway for that customer
- route new sessions to quantized variant redwood-small-v1-quant in us-west-2
- schedule rolling restarts of a small subset (canary) to defragment GPUs

rahul: to add: cap per-session KV entries to 1024 via runtime config (hotpatchable). Also expose a metric for "kv_entries_per_session" and alarm on sustained growth.

alex: customer agreed to try routing to quantized and enabling TTL for a few hours.

k8s-bot: RollingUpdate started on inference-workers-us-west-2; 5 pods will be restarted.

rahul: canary results: after routing + canary restarts p95 for the affected sessions dropped from ~420ms -> ~140ms within 3 minutes. p99 improved but still had tails at ~700-900ms during heavy KV churn.
dave: good sign. quantized variant reduces memory footprint so less fragmentation; TTL prevents unbounded growth.

nina: medium-term fixes we should track:
- implement allocator compaction API that can be triggered during safe windows
- switch to slab-style allocator for small allocations to reduce fragmentation
- implement proactive circuit-breaker in runtime to evict least-recently-used session fragments when fragmentation ratio exceeds threshold
- add alerting for allocator retry rate and fragmentation ratio

rahul: created RFC for slab allocator evolution (RDW-1302). Created ops tasks: RDW-1303 (kv caps + TTL), RDW-1304 (metrics+alerts), RDW-1305 (routing fallback policy).

alex: notes for support response to customer: cause = KV cache growth + GPU memory fragmentation causing allocator retries and host spills -> higher token latency. Applied mitigations: temporarily routed traffic to quantized model, enabled session TTL, and performed targeted worker restarts. Working on permanent allocator improvements.

nina: can someone paste the repro script or gist here?
dave: gist: https://gist.internal/kv-frag-repro-2028-07

rahul: quick config we toggled (example):
```
# runtime config
kv_session_ttl_seconds=30
kv_max_entries_per_session=1024
routing_override.C-998=redwood-small-v1-quant
```

alex: follow-ups: keep this thread open for 48h of stable metrics. If fragmentation reappears, we will schedule a maintenance window for allocator compaction.

ops-bot: Deploy job 89212 succeeded: restarted 5 inference-worker pods in us-west-2
k8s-bot: pod inference-worker-7c9 restarted at 04:38:12 UTC

nina: thanks team. filing a short postmortem once we have 24h of stable telemetry. adding an action to docs: "customer guidance on long-lived sessions and kv cache".

dave: one more operational note: we should add a runtime metric that exposes the largest contiguous free GPU block size (largest_free_block_bytes). That'll help predict when large allocations will fail even with enough total free memory.

alex: agreed. marking done: temporary mitigations applied. Owners: rahul (ops tasks), nina (customer comms), dave (allocator metrics), alex (postmortem).
